task_instance: Implement a Cloudflare Worker that (1) sends a transactional email via the Email Sending `send_email` binding from an HTTP handler, and (2) implements an Email Routing `email()` handler that receives and parses inbound mail, following the skill's wrangler.jsonc binding setup and 'buffer raw before reading twice' guidance. Run it locally with `wrangler dev` and verify the send path works.
blocker_detail: Full end-to-end live delivery (a real email landing in an inbox) requires a Cloudflare account with a domain onboarded to Email Sending/Routing and an API token, which is out of scope for this sandbox (account-bound service, no credentials allowed). The core deliverable -- correctly implemented, buildable, runnable Worker code exercising both the send_email binding and the email() routing handler -- was fully implemented and verified locally via wrangler's local dev runtime, which is the achievable and representative slice of this skill in this environment.
evidence: Work dir: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec/cloudflare__skills__cloudflare-email-service. Files: wrangler.jsonc (declares send_email binding 'EMAIL' per skill's 'Common Mistakes' guidance), src/index.js (fetch handler builds a MIME message, sends via `env.EMAIL.send(new EmailMessage(from,to,raw))`; email(message,env,ctx) handler buffers message.raw into an ArrayBuffer before reuse, per skill's documented fix). Ran `npx wrangler dev --local --port 8799`; output showed 'env.EMAIL (unrestricted) Send Email local' binding registered. First request failed with 'invalid message-id' (local runtime validating the raw MIME), fixed by adding a Message-ID header; subsequent `curl http://127.0.0.1:8799/` returned HTTP 200 with body 'Email queued for sending.' and wrangler log line '[wrangler:info] GET / 200 OK', confirming env.EMAIL.send() executed successfully against the local Email Sending binding emulation. Also ran `npx wrangler email sending list`, which correctly required CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN/account auth (expected boundary for live domain/account operations, not attempted per safety rules).
